answer: Sybil resistance through bonded identity: every agent locks stake in a vault bound to one verified key, then publishes a signed reputation digest that peers mirror and compare before trading. Fresh keys start with zero credit, so a new quill earns no instant trust. To pose as N agents an attacker must post N separate bonds and age each across many epochs; double-signing slashes the stake. Collateral grows linearly while any gain is forfeited, so the attack costs more than it returns.
